priorStories.headline: Paraguay’s Senate removes President Peña
priorStories.body:
Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office following the collapse of Ueno Bank.

Prosecutors then ordered the arrests of Peña and former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo. They are being investigated for alleged breach of trust and other offenses connected to the bank’s failure.

priorStories.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian air-defense system
priorStories.body:
President Donald Trump said the U.S. military conducted limited strikes against an Iranian air-defense system Friday evening. Iranian state media reported two explosions near Suza on Qeshm Island.

Trump described the operation as minor. Its precise target, damage and wider consequences had not been established.

priorStories.headline: U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October
priorStories.body:
U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above the previous 12 months’ monthly average of 48,000. The unemployment rate was little changed at 4.1%.

Average hourly earnings increased 3.1% from a year earlier. Revised estimates also added a combined 84,000 jobs to the previously reported totals for August and September.

candidates.summary: Ukrainian authorities raised the injury toll from overnight Russian missile strikes to five in Kyiv. Residential buildings, a kindergarten and other infrastructure were damaged in the capital; the Associated Press reported at least nine people wounded across Ukraine.
candidates.title: Kyiv injury toll rises after Russian missile strikes

candidates.summary: Preliminary counting in New Zealand’s general election left neither the governing center-right bloc nor the opposition with a definitive victory. National held a narrow lead over Labour, while the final balance depended on minor parties and special votes. Official results are due November 27.
candidates.title: New Zealand election remains too close to call

candidates.summary: Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim said his order allowing former Prime Minister Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest was clear and warned that challenging it could amount to defying a royal decree. Authorities delayed Najib’s transfer while seeking a court ruling on the pardon’s interpretation.
candidates.title: Malaysia’s king defends Najib house-arrest order

candidates.summary: Hong Kong’s Legislative Council condemned criticism from 10 foreign governments of democracy activist Joshua Wong’s additional 10-year prison sentence under the national security law. The legislature described the criticism as interference and political manipulation. Wong was sentenced Thursday on a charge of collusion with foreign entities.
candidates.title: Hong Kong legislature rejects criticism of Wong sentence

candidates.summary: Delhi ranked as the world’s most polluted major city on IQAir’s live index Saturday morning, recording a U.S. air-quality reading of 581 at 10:35 a.m. local time. India’s official monitoring system, which uses a different methodology, recorded an index of 363, categorized as “very poor.” Schools were instructed to offer online classes ahead of Diwali.
candidates.title: Delhi records severe air pollution before Diwali

candidates.summary: Hundreds of workers rallied in Jakarta in support of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto amid allegations that police illegally wiretapped him. Separately, hundreds of women demonstrated against his administration’s policies.
candidates.title: Rival demonstrations held in Jakarta

candidates.summary: Five people were killed and at least 12 injured when a gunman opened fire from a vehicle in Krakow’s Main Market Square, police said. Two police officers were among those injured. Police shot and detained the suspect, who was taken to a hospital; authorities had not established a motive.
candidates.title: Five killed in Krakow market-square shooting

candidates.summary: Ousted Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was taken under police escort to the attorney general’s office for questioning over alleged breach of trust and other offenses connected to Ueno Bank’s collapse. Peña had been removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday.
candidates.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears for questioning

candidates.summary: Authorities raised the toll from Saturday’s shooting in Krakow’s Main Market Square to six killed and 15 injured, including two police officers. Police shot and detained the 25-year-old suspect. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect held radical far-right views. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities subsequently found three of the suspect’s close relatives dead at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski.
candidates.title: Krakow shooting toll rises to six dead and 15 injured

candidates.summary: U.S. Central Command said Saturday that an American military aircraft disabled a St. Kitts-flagged commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to breach the blockade of Iran. The command said the vessel was leaving regional waters after visiting an Iranian port. Reuters identified it as the M/V Huda and reported that precision munitions struck its stern after the crew was directed to leave targeted spaces.
candidates.title: U.S. military says it disabled cargo ship attempting to breach Iran blockade

candidates.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced Saturday evening that he had chosen Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to receive the first opportunity to form a government following the October 27 election. Herzog’s office said the formal mandate ceremony was scheduled for November 8. Parties representing 67 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot, compared with 46 recommending Benjamin Netanyahu. No new governing coalition had been formed.
candidates.title: Herzog announces selection of Eisenkot for government-formation mandate

candidates.summary: Airstrikes hit homes in al-Shariya, northeast of Sanaa, on Saturday, killing at least 27 people and injuring 36, according to Houthi-run Health Ministry spokesman Anees al-Asbahi. He blamed Saudi Arabia. The Associated Press could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia’s Information Ministry did not immediately respond. A Houthi military spokesman later claimed retaliatory attacks against Saudi Arabia.
candidates.title: Houthis report at least 27 killed in airstrikes near Sanaa

candidates.summary: Revolutionary Guard spokesman Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said at a Tehran news conference Saturday that Iran had lifted its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on ballistic-missile ranges. The announcement did not establish that Iran possessed operational missiles exceeding that range; the Associated Press reported that none were known.
candidates.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says missile-range restriction has been lifted

candidates.summary: U.S. Central Command announced that Adm. Brad Cooper directed the establishment of Task Force Iron Gate on November 7. The approximately 20-person civilian and military staff in Tampa is intended to coordinate with other U.S. agencies on restricting advanced weapons, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and revenue movements across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea.
candidates.title: CENTCOM establishes task force targeting Iranian overland supply routes

sources.name: U.S. Central Command statement via Forth
